question: Project 19 (REASSEMBLE CRPS L2 skill segmentation): the champion GRUctx|lag3 beats SF|lag3 by +0.0418 Segmental F1 (0.7135 vs 0.6717) and by +0.0623 over the capacity-matched DualHead (0.6468) on 111 DEV episodes / 17 objects / 5 recordings. Is that increment caused by explicitly aligned predicted parent-action fusion rather than by extra capacity, longer history or action-label supervision, and does it survive recording-level resampling and a cross-recording (sealed) replication?

scope.input: frozen DEV predictions + frozen sealed predictions
scope.grouping: recording date (5 clusters), object LODO folds

probes.observable: episode-clustered paired delta Segmental F1 (GRUctx|lag3 minus capacity-matched DualHead|lag3 and minus SF|lag3) recomputed from frozen DEV predictions
probes.comparison_reference: same frozen DEV predictions, capacity-matched DualHead|lag3 and no-context SF|lag3, no new training

probes.observable: sealed 37-episode paired delta Segmental F1 (GRUctx|lag3 minus SF|lag3) with one full-DEV model, plus per-recording and per-object signs
probes.comparison_reference: same single full-DEV model, SF|lag3 head on the same sealed frames
